versions.notes:
**Changed**

- **A piece is your whole setup, saved as a file.** **Menu → Export as a piece…**
  saves every device that isn't Unassigned (its name, its calibration and the
  preset it plays) together with those presets, as a `.mugic` file. **Import
  piece…** adds the presets to your list, then asks which of your devices plays
  each device of the piece; your other devices are set to Unassigned. If you
  already have a preset of the same name with other settings, choose **Use
  existing** (keeps your own changes), **Replace**, or **Keep both**.
- **Presets have their own file.** **Menu → Export current preset…** saves the
  selected preset as a `.mugicset` file; **Import preset…** adds one (replace
  yours or keep both) and selects it on this device.
- The Preset menu lists presets only; pieces no longer appear in it.
- **A Main Menu in the header** gathers these, the standalone app's Audio/MIDI
  settings and Save / Load / Reset state, and Help (which replaces the **?**).
- **Tooltips work on iPad.** Hover over a control for a moment, or press and hold
  it on iPad (holding doesn't press it). New tips on the Map tab's gear and
  **LEARN** buttons, the column labels and the tabs; a disabled **LEARN** says why.
- **Menu → Settings…** turns tooltips on or off and sets the battery reading (the
  same choice as on the Device tab). Settings apply to every project.
- **Typing a CC on the Map tab:** clicking the box selects it, so typing
  replaces it. Only **Enter** applies what you typed; **Esc** (or clicking
  away) puts the previous choice back, and an edit not yet applied is outlined
  in orange.
- **Menu → New preset from current…** replaces the **Save as…** button, which
  made the bar overflow. It asks for the name in a dialog and says so before
  replacing a preset of the same name.

**Fixed**

- **The steadiness window is part of the preset.** Switching presets now sets
  it (Default sets 5 s). A preset saved before keeps the device's current
  window until you change the window once with that preset selected.
- When a tab or the Main Menu doesn't fit the window, a scrollbar now shows from
  the start, not only once you scroll (on iPad, a ▾ at the bottom: tap it to
  scroll). Before, an open Energy settings panel looked complete with Jolt and
  **Play hard** cut off below.
- **Import piece…**: a device added with **+ Add device** now plays the piece
  device it was added for. Before, it stayed on Default (and wasn't chosen in
  the dialog), and only devices you already had got the piece's settings.
- **The Preset menu says when a device's mapping isn't its preset's:** **Default
  (edited)** after changing a row on Default, or **“name” (not in list)** when
  its preset is gone (a project from an older version can load that way). Pick
  a preset to use it, or **New preset from current…** to keep the mapping.
- **Export as a piece…** no longer adds a "<device> mapping" preset for a device
  whose mapping is one of your presets (or Default) under another name: the
  piece says it plays that preset. Devices sharing a new mapping share one.
- **Esc** in a number box now puts the old value back; before, it kept what
  you had typed.
- The export and import dialogs open in the folder you last used for a piece or
  preset (as Save / Load state does), not always in Documents.
- Exporting no longer depends on what is selected in the Preset menu: before,
  a preset played by four devices exported with only the selected one in it.

**Note:** `.mugic` files from 2.3.0 can't be opened; export them again.

**New**

- **Pieces: one setup for every performer.** A piece holds all your devices at
  once — each device is a *part* ("Violin 1", "Cello") with its mapping and
  calibration. Name your devices after the parts, then **⋯ → Save all devices
  as piece…**. Picking a piece sets up every device in one go; devices that
  aren't in it send nothing.
- **Share a piece as a `.mugic` file.** **⋯ → Export…** saves it; **⋯ →
  Import…** adds it to your list (nothing else is removed) and asks which of
  your devices plays each part, whatever their names or ports. A name you
  already have can be replaced or kept alongside.
- **Pieces remember your changes**, calibration included, so you can
  re-calibrate an imported piece for yourself and keep it.
- **Update notice.** When a newer version is out, the version next to
  *MUGIC MOTION* turns pink; click it to open the download page.

**Fixed**

- **Loading a saved state shows it right away.** The window used to keep the
  previous mapping and preset list, and your next edit could write them back
  (bringing deleted presets back).
- **Out is remembered.** The MIDI **Out** choice is saved with your project or
  saved state instead of going back to *DAW (Host)*; if that port isn't there,
  it falls back to *DAW (Host)*.

**New**

- **MUGIC MOTION Plugin for iPad.** The plugin now runs on iPad (iPadOS 16
  or later) as an **Audio Unit (AUv3) MIDI effect** — add it in a music app
  that hosts MIDI effects, such as Loopy Pro, and route its MIDI to any
  instrument, just like on your computer. It also works as a standalone app. iPad
  testers get it through TestFlight.
- **Keeps playing in the background (iPad).** The standalone app keeps
  receiving your MUGIC and sending MIDI while another app is in front.
- **MUGIC as a MIDI source for other apps.** In the standalone app on Mac
  and iPad, **Out** now offers *MUGIC MOTION (virtual port)*. Choose it and
  any other app — a synth app on iPad, a DAW on Mac — can select
  "MUGIC MOTION" as its MIDI input. On Mac you no longer need the IAC Driver
  for this.

**Good to know (iPad)**

- The plugin and the standalone app both listen on the same network port
  (4000), so use one at a time: close the standalone app before opening
  the plugin in your music app, or restart the music app if the plugin
  shows no motion.
- MUGIC sends controllers and pitch bend, not notes: play notes on a
  keyboard (on-screen or MIDI) and shape them with your movements.

**Fixed**

- **iPad: you can change what each movement sends.** On iPad the "Sends as"
  box (for example *modulation (CC 1)*) couldn't be changed, especially in
  Loopy Pro. It is now a menu: tap it and pick pitch bend, a named
  controller, or any CC number from 0 to 127. On Mac and Windows nothing
  changes: you can still type into the box.

**Improved**

- **Preset menu grows with the window.** Making the plugin window wider now
  widens the Preset menu (and the name box when saving a preset), so long
  preset names fit, instead of leaving an empty gap next to the tabs.

**Fixed**

- **Runs on macOS 11 Big Sur and later again.** 2.1.0 (and recent builds
  before it) only opened on the newest macOS (26 Tahoe); on older versions
  — including Apple Silicon Macs such as M3 on Sonoma or Sequoia — the app
  would not launch and the AU/VST3 would not load in your DAW.

**New**

- **High-resolution (14-bit) CC.** Any output sent as CC 0–31 can now go out
  in 16,384 steps instead of 128, for smooth sweeps with no audible stepping on
  filters and other sensitive controls. Click the small **14** next to *Sends
  as*, or type a **+** after the number (e.g. `14+`). It is sent as the
  standard pair — CC 14 with CC 46, CC 1 with CC 33, and so on — so use it only
  with synths and DAWs that support 14-bit CC. Off by default; existing
  projects and presets are unchanged.

**New**

- The battery voltage now appears next to the percentage, at the top of the
  window and on the Device tab (e.g. *≈100% · 4.22 V*). The *≈* means the
  percentage is estimated from the voltage.
- **Battery** menu on the Device tab: *from voltage* (the default) or the
  *device's reading*. Even on the device's reading, the plug-in switches to the
  estimate if the reading doesn't match the voltage. Click its *?* for details.

**Fixed**

- **Battery reads right when the MUGIC® is full.** A fully charged MUGIC®
  showed only about 85%. The charge is now worked out from the battery voltage,
  the same way the MUGIC® Max app does, so the two agree.

**New**

- **The whole window scales.** Make the window bigger and the text, buttons and
  axis pictures grow with it — drag the corner grip if the text is too small.
- **Toggle mode** for every output, beside *Continuous* and *Switch*: each time
  the motion rises past the crossing point, the output flips on or off. One jolt
  turns sustain on, the next turns it off. Click the mode button to choose.
- **JOLT** is now simply **Momentary** (on during the jolt) or **Toggle** (one
  jolt on, the next off). Jolt is only ever on or off, so it no longer offers
  *Continuous* or a crossing point.

**Changed**

- Jolt's *Trigger: toggle* setting has become the **Toggle** mode on the Jolt
  row; projects that used it switch over automatically.

**New**

- The standalone app has its own icon: the MUGIC® μ, marked **PLUGIN**, so it's
  easy to tell apart from the MUGIC app and other MUGIC software.
- The μ logo at the top of the window is now sharp at any size.

**New**

- **Clear log**, next to *Show log file* (Device tab and the help window). For a
  bug report: clear the log, make the problem happen again, then send the log.
  The log is plain text, so you can also trim it before sending.

A redesigned, much smaller window — and six new things MUGIC® can send as MIDI.

**New**

- **Speed and steadiness as MIDI.** Each of YAW, PITCH and ROLL can now also send
  how fast it's moving and how long it has held a direction. Open them with the
  arrow next to the axis on the **Map** tab. They start off unassigned, so your
  existing setup sends nothing new until you map them.
- **A smaller window you can resize.** It opens at a compact size and you can drag
  the corner grip to make it bigger; your project remembers the size and the tab
  you were on.
- **Three tabs.** **Calibrate** (opens first: it shows what yaw, pitch and roll
  mean), **Map** (what each motion sends) and **Device** (port, prefix, adding
  devices).
- **One row per output.** Each row shows the live motion, the MIDI value being
  sent, and a **Sends as** box: type a CC number or pick a named controller or
  pitch bend.
- **Settings on each row** (the sliders button): MIDI Min / Max, channel, and how
  that motion is measured.
- **Calibrate speed** — move as fast as you play and it sets that axis's full
  speed.
- **Energy: Rest and Play hard** set Low and High from your own playing.
- **Jolt: see the signal** against the threshold, and **Suggest threshold** from a
  few seconds of normal playing and three jolts.
- **Calibration length** — 5 seconds by default, longer if you need more time to
  reach the extremes.
- Steadiness has its own window for each axis.
- **Show log file** is on the Device tab and at the bottom of the help window,
  for sending us a bug report.

**Changed**

- Calibrating an axis: click **Calibrate YAW** (or PITCH, ROLL) right on the
  Calibrate tab; orange marks show the range you reached.
- **MIDI ON/OFF** is at the top right and belongs to the selected device, as
  before.
- Speed is now measured in degrees per second, so it no longer depends on how
  fast the device streams.
- Your saved presets carry over; presets saved now also keep MIDI Min / Max.

**Removed**

- The *Device* pause switch and the Orientation bars, replaced by the live meters
  on each row.

**New**

- The version number is shown next to *MUGIC MOTION* at the top of the window.

**Fixed**

- **Calibrate Motion** no longer hides the axis cards and Orientation bars: its
  window now sits at the bottom, so you can watch what you're calibrating.

**Changed**

- **Noise Floor** (in the Jolt panel) now affects Jolt only. It used to quietly
  apply to Energy as well, even though Energy has no Noise Floor setting. Energy's
  **Low** already does that job: anything at or below Low sends 0. At the default
  setting you won't hear a difference.

**New**

- A settings wheel on **YAW**, **PITCH** and **ROLL** with **MIDI Min** and
  **MIDI Max** (0 and 127 by default), also added to the Energy and Jolt panels.
  Each parameter then sends only over that range; set Min above Max to invert.
- The number on each axis card is now the MIDI value actually sent.
- No more **ASSIGN**: every change takes effect immediately. The button under
  each parameter is now just **LEARN**.
- The log now records what you do: MIDI mappings, presets, MIDI on/off and
  routing, devices and calibration.
- **Show log file** is also in the **Instructions** panel.

**Fixed**

- Pitch bend was off by half its range: a level ROLL sent full bend down and
  jumped to full up past the middle. It now runs smoothly from full down to full
  up, centred at rest.
- The **MIDI PARAM** menu and the **CC#** number always agree: type 10 and the
  menu shows *pan (CC 10)*; *none* always shows 0 (*off* in Numerical mode).
- *Unassigned* no longer leaves the Default numbers behind.
- Typing a CC# no longer sends the numbers on the way (typing 64 never sends 6).

**New**

- **Show log file**: click **?** next to *MUGIC MOTION*, at the bottom of the
  panel. Send the file with any bug report.
- How to get MUGIC's MIDI into **Ableton Live** and **Logic Pro** (in
  Instructions and the install guide).
- **Unassigned** preset (from 1.3.0, not released separately): mutes all five
  parameters, a blank slate to map up from.

**Fixed**

- MUGIC could stop moving after a while until the plug-in was reloaded; it now
  reconnects on its own.
- A device whose port was busy at startup is picked up once the port is free.
- The battery shows **—** with no data and **Calibrating…** just after power-on,
  instead of **0%**.
- Slimmer title bar; more room below the **LEARN** buttons.

You can now type MIDI CC numbers in directly, instead of picking them from a menu.

- A **PARAM MODE** selector sits between **MIDI OUT TO** and **CHANNEL**.
  **Presets** is the plug-in as you know it — the named MIDI PARAM menus plus
  CUSTOM CC#. **Numerical** replaces each menu with a single **MIDI CC#** box
  (0–127), for when you already know the controller numbers you want.
- Switching between the two modes never rewrites a mapping. Type a number that
  matches a named preset and the name comes back, so flipping to Presets reads
  "pan (CC 10)" rather than "custom CC#".
- Clearing the box mutes that parameter, so muting stays one keystroke away in
  Numerical mode.
- The instructions panel inside the plug-in documents both modes.

**Fixed:** Device sometimes went quiet when the plug-in was reloaded without
restarting the host — reopening a session, or restarting the SuperCollider
server — even though the **MIDI OUT** button still read **MIDI ON**.
The **MIDI OUT** button now always shows what the plug-in is really doing,
including when your DAW changes it through automation.

The install instructions were corrected too: MUGIC MOTION is an **instrument**
(AU / VST3), so load it on an instrument track — it never appears under audio
effects — and your host lists it as **MUGIC MOTION**, not KIMARI.

The macOS installer is signed and notarized by Apple, and universal for Intel and
Apple Silicon.

The plug-in's controls are now visible to your DAW, so they can be automated or mapped to a MIDI controller.

- **Reset Orientation**, **Reset Wrap** and **Reset Range Cal** can be mapped to a button or footswitch, per device or for all devices at once — re-centre mid-performance without touching the computer.
- **MIDI Out** can be switched per device from the DAW, as a per-device mute.
- The resets are momentary: a button that sends on-press / off-release fires them once per press.

Motion itself (yaw, pitch, roll, energy, jolt) still leaves the plug-in as MIDI CC and pitch bend, exactly as before.

The macOS installer is signed and notarized by Apple, and universal for Intel and Apple Silicon.
